Ravi: Quick RFC follow-up9: proposing an ingress compatibility-bridge (ICB) to accept deprecated API shapes and emit the new runtime contract. Opt-in per-tenant flag; header-gated. Purpose: reduce client breakage during vNext rollout.
Maya: +1 for opt-in. Main worry is streaming semantics. Legacy clients stream raw text frames; new runtime streams structured events. Do we reframe at the gateway or keep a conversion layer in the runtime?
Theo: I built a tiny PoC that does framing at the gateway. For non-streams it's trivial. Streaming conversion at edge costs ~3-6ms p99 on our test rig for 2KB chunks. Adds ~0.8ms median.
Ravi: Important: double-serialize risk if we reframe at edge and runtime also tries to normalize. We need a clear ownership: gateway does translation OR runtime treats X-ICB-Applied header as a signal to skip normalization.
Maya: Agree. Propose header handshake: X-ICB: active and X-ICB-Mode: permissive|strict. If active, runtime checks X-ICB-Applied and skips its mapping. If missing, runtime falls back to its compatibility layer.
Theo: Pseudocode from PoC:
```
if header 'X-ICB' == 'legacy->current':
  if request.is_streaming():
    first = read_frame()
    mapped_meta = map_metadata(first)
    emit(mapped_meta as header-frame)
    for f in remaining_frames: emit(map_frame(f))
  else:
    mapped = transform(json_body)
    if mapped.ok: forward(mapped) else: if tenant.strict: return 422 else: forward(original with X-ICB-Warn)
```
Ravi: Good. Telemetry we want: icb_invoked, icb_latency_ms, icb_stream_rewrites, icb_error_rate. Tag by tenant_id and endpoint route. Also trace id propagation.
Maya: Cache key compatibility is a big one. If field names change, existing prefix caches will miss. Two options: canonicalize keys post-translation to match old keys OR store a mapping table in the cache layer. Canonicalization seems simpler but brittle.
Theo: Agreed. My recommendation: compute canonical_cache_key(input, stable_schema_map) for both bridge and runtime. Add key aliasing where safe. Monitor cache_miss_delta after rollout.
ops-bot: Created alert rule 'icb_error_rate' -> notify on-call if >1% over 5m for >=3 tenants. Dashboard panel 'Ingress Compatibility Bridge - invocations/latency' added.
Ravi: Security: transformations must be declarative and white-listed. No templating, no regex-eval that could be exploited. sec-bot please run the transformation audit.
sec-bot: Will run audit. Also require that any field redaction rules are applied before logging. No tenant secrets should be retained in any transformed payloads.
Maya: Rollout plan suggestion: internal dev tenants (2) -> platform partners (8) -> 25 tenants -> broad. Canary gates: icb_error_rate, p99 latency delta, cache_hit_ratio change. Rollback: flip tenant flag off or remove filter from ingress route.
Theo: One more: tool-calling param renames. For renamed tool args we should provide aliasing mapping in the tool registry layer as a stopgap. Otherwise downstream tools will get mis-named args.
Ravi: For ambiguous mappings (freeform->structured), default to pass-through with X-ICB-Note header warn and optionally store original payload tombstone (S3 pointer) if tenant enables debug. Explicit strict-mode should reject ambiguous translations.
Maya: Also add an opt-out TTL and RBAC around who can flip the opt-in flag. Platform-release + tenant-ops roles only.
Theo: I'll produce a compact Envoy/WASM filter sketch and perf numbers (ETA 48h). Ravi: can you draft the rollout playbook and mapping whitelist (ETA 24h)? Maya: you'll own security checklist and RBAC changes (ETA 48h)?
Ravi: Yep. Action items summarized: Theo -> prototype + perf (48h), Ravi -> playbook + whitelist (24h), Maya -> security + RBAC (48h). Revisit next week. :white_check_mark:
